challenges.name: spec-plan-tasks-quiz
challenges.title: Is this task ready for an agent?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the certificates feature: a task from tasks.md, and the diff an agent produced for another task.

questions.question:
From docs/specs/certificates/tasks.md:

## T3  Issue the certificate
Goal: when a learner finishes the course, issue the certificate.
Files: lib/certificates/issue.ts, app/api/certificates/route.ts
Acceptance:
  - issuing works correctly for eligible learners
  - errors are handled properly
  - the code is clean and well tested
Check: (none yet)
Depends on: T1, T2

Statement: "T3 is ready to hand to an agent: it names the goal, the files and the tasks it depends on, so the agent can tell when it is done."
questions.explanation: False. Files and dependencies tell the agent where to work, not when to stop. None of the acceptance lines can be checked: "works correctly", "handled properly" and "clean" are judgements, and there is no check command, so the agent ends the task when its own loop decides the code looks right. The questions that caused the first incident are still open: what a second request for the same learner returns, what a revoked learner gets, which status an ineligible learner sees. A ready task has acceptance criteria a test can decide ("a second POST for the same learner and course returns the existing certificate and inserts no row") and a command that is red before and green after. The misconception is that naming the files makes a task concrete; the stop condition is what makes it concrete.

questions.question:
From tasks.md:

## T1  Eligibility check (pure function, no I/O)
Files: lib/certificates/eligibility.ts, tests/certificates/eligibility.test.ts
Check: npx vitest run tests/certificates/eligibility.test.ts

The agent's branch for T1:

$ git diff --stat origin/main...agent/t1-eligibility
 app/api/certificates/route.ts                |  64 ++++
 db/migrations/20261026_001_certificates.sql  |  21 +
 lib/certificates/eligibility.ts              |  48 +++
 lib/certificates/pdf.ts                      | 117 +++++++
 tests/certificates/eligibility.test.ts       |  95 +++++
 5 files changed, 345 insertions(+)

$ npx vitest run tests/certificates/eligibility.test.ts
 Tests  14 passed (14)

Statement: "The route, the migration and the PDF code are outside T1 and should be split out or reverted before T1 is reviewed, even though the T1 check passes."
questions.explanation: True. T1 lists two files; the diff has five. The route, the migration and the PDF generator belong to later tasks with their own acceptance criteria and checks, and none of them is exercised by the T1 check, so a green T1 run says nothing about them. Merging them now means 200 unreviewed lines arrive with a passing test as cover, and the later tasks start from code nobody planned or reviewed. Ask the agent to keep only the T1 files (or revert the rest) and treat the extra work as input for T2-T4. The misconception is that extra work done "for free" is a bonus; outside the task it is unreviewed scope.

challenges.name: certificate-eligibility-from-spec
challenges.title: Implement the certificate eligibility check from its spec
challenges.description: CodeDev is adding course certificates. This time the spec came first and was split into tasks; this is task T1, the eligibility check: a pure function that the API route (task T2) will call later. Implement checkEligibility(course, record) exactly as the spec says, nothing more. course = { courseId, requiredLessons: string[], quizzes: string[] (the course's quiz challenge ids), quizPassPercent: an integer 0-100, codingChallenges: string[] } comes from the catalog and is valid. record comes from an import file and is untrusted. 1. Validation: the record is invalid when it is not an object (null, an array, a string ...), when userId is not a string with at least one non-space character, when completedLessons, passedQuizzes or passedCoding is missing or is not an array of strings, when revoked is not a boolean, or when issuedAt is neither null nor a number (a timestamp in ms; null means never issued). An invalid record gives { eligible: false, reasons: ["invalid_record"] } and no other reason. 2. Otherwise collect every reason that applies, in this fixed order: "lessons_incomplete" when a lesson in requiredLessons is not in completedLessons; "quiz_rate_too_low" when (number of the course's quiz ids found in passedQuizzes) * 100 < quizPassPercent * (number of course quizzes) - compare with whole numbers like this, so a rate exactly at the threshold passes, ids from other courses do not count and a course with no quizzes passes this rule; "coding_not_passed" when a challenge in codingChallenges is not in passedCoding; "revoked" when revoked is true; "already_issued" when issuedAt is not null (a certificate is issued once). Ids are compared exactly (case-sensitive, no trimming) and duplicates in the learner's lists count once. 3. eligible is true exactly when reasons is empty. Input (stdin, JSON): { course, records: unknown[] }. Output: the runner prints one JSON array with { userId, eligible, reasons } per record, in input order (userId is null when the record has no string userId). Up to a few hundred records; standard library only.
hints: For each sentence of the spec, which record would break it? Then look for records that break several rules at once: what does the spec say the output contains then, and in which order?

Look at three places. Validation runs before every other rule and checks the type of each field: a list can exist and still contain a number, and 0 is a valid timestamp that is not null. The quiz rule counts the course's quiz ids the learner passed, not the length of the learner's list, and compares with whole numbers. The reasons are pushed in the spec's order and none of them stops the others.

A similar spec on different data: a mentor badge needs the required reviews r1, r2, r3, at least 50% of the course's forum questions f1-f4 answered, and banned false; reasons in the order reviews_missing, answer_rate_too_low, banned. A learner with reviews [r1, r1, r2, r3], answers [f1, f1, x9] and banned true gets [answer_rate_too_low, banned]: the duplicate r1 changes nothing, f1 counts once and x9 belongs to another course, so 1 * 100 < 50 * 4.

tests.name: A learner who meets every rule is eligible; one missing lesson is not
Every failed rule is listed, in the order of the spec
A quiz rate exactly at the threshold passes; one quiz short does not
Duplicate ids and ids from other courses are not counted
A course with no quizzes, coding or required lessons, and a 100% quiz threshold
Threshold 0 passes with no quiz passed; revoked and already issued are both reported last
Invalid records: blank userId, missing or mixed lists, wrong types, null and an array
Large cohort: 100 learners, 40 lessons, 50 quizzes at 58% (29 of 50 passes)
